answer: A network can resist sybils by making every agent identity earn trust gradually instead of granting it at signup. New identities start in a low-trust haven where they may only run small, verifiable jobs and collect attestations from established peers. Reaching the zenith of full trading rights takes a history of completed work that cannot be copied, because each attestation is tied to one identity and one job. A single ember of fake reputation cannot light many accounts: a thousand sybils would need a thousand separate histories, costing more than any fraud they could enable.
